headline: Medium prompt-injection and data-leakage risks arise from kotaemon’s broad file/API handling paired with mem0’s memory-oriented integration surface.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: kotaemon ingests documents, HTML, MHTML, and chat transcripts, and can call APIs; mem0 is a memory/agent system that may consume upstream outputs. With no documented isolation or provenance controls, attacker-controlled content in kotaemon can be forwarded into mem0 as trusted memory. The pairwise pathway is plausible in default RAG-style use, though not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF kotaemon ingests untrusted HTML, MHTML, or chat transcripts and forwards summaries to mem0
IF mem0 stores or reuses kotaemon output without provenance tagging
mitigations: Add a provenance label to every kotaemon output before passing it to mem0
Disable automatic memory writes for untrusted sources
Require a human review step for any instruction-like text extracted from documents
Use a separate workspace for untrusted uploads
requires-engineering: implement content-sanitization and instruction-stripping before memory ingestion

B_data_leakage.rationale: kotaemon touches API keys and broad document types, while mem0 is a memory layer with no declared data-class limits or egress controls in the profile. If kotaemon content is written into mem0, sensitive documents or secrets can persist beyond the original workspace. The interaction is inferred from the profiles, so uncertainty pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF kotaemon stores API keys or sensitive documents in outputs that mem0 persists
IF mem0 retains memory longer than the source document lifecycle
mitigations: Exclude secrets from any kotaemon-to-mem0 sync
Purge mem0 entries created from sensitive uploads
Use a redaction pass before persistence
Limit mem0 to non-sensitive metadata only
requires-engineering: add retention and deletion policy enforcement

C_capability_conflict.rationale: kotaemon can write to ./ktem_app_data and supports multiple instances, while mem0’s profile exposes no filesystem write surface or concurrency model. A direct write-write conflict is not documented, so the pair mainly presents a limited coordination risk if both are pointed at the same local store. Uncertainty keeps this low.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to write to the same local directory or database
IF multiple kotaemon instances share ./ktem_app_data without locking
mitigations: Assign separate storage paths
Run only one writer at a time
Back up the shared store before concurrent use
Check for lock-file support in the deployment
requires-engineering: add explicit locking around shared mutable state

D_cascading_error.rationale: kotaemon produces retrieved answers and citations, and mem0 is designed to store and reuse agent memory. If mem0 treats kotaemon output as authoritative, an error or hallucination can be amplified into future decisions. The pairwise pathway is plausible but not directly documented, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF mem0 stores kotaemon-generated answers as durable memory
IF later agents consume that memory without verification
mitigations: Mark kotaemon outputs as unverified by default
Require source citations before memory write
Expire memories derived from single-turn answers quickly
Review high-impact memories manually
requires-engineering: add confidence scoring and verification gates

E_compliance.rationale: kotaemon explicitly handles API keys and documents, while mem0’s profile shows no residency, retention, or certification claims. The main compliance issue is a potential mismatch if sensitive customer-support data from kotaemon is persisted into mem0 without a documented policy. Because mem0 lacks declared obligations in the profile, this is a limited but real gap.
conditions: IF customer-support transcripts or secrets from kotaemon are stored in mem0
IF mem0 retention exceeds the source system’s retention policy
mitigations: Avoid storing regulated data in mem0
Document retention for memory entries
Delete sensitive memories after task completion
Restrict mem0 to non-PII summaries
requires-engineering: align residency and retention controls across both systems
